newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Hamas activists seek clearer course, new leaders.
newsitem.headline: Hamas activists seek clearer course, new leaders.

text.p: Many members of the Islamic Resistance Movement Hamas in Gaza are asking its leaders to step down so the group can chart a new, clear course, Hamas activists said on Thursday.

"We don't know what Hamas' strategy is anymore. We are lost on very important issues: Do we want to stop military activities? Do we want a dialogue or confrontation with the Palestinian Authority?" one activist said.

Hamas members have been locked in months of internal debate over the future of the movement, whose suicide bombings in Israel in February and March touched off a crackdown against Islamists by Palestinian self-rule authorities.
Hundreds of Hamas supporters were arrested and many complained of having been tortured by Palestinian security forces.

Activists cited ideological differences and a struggle between the traditional leadership of the Moslem Brotherhood, Hamas' parent group, and the young, rebellious generation active during the Palestinian uprising against Israeli occupation.
Several young Hamas activists told Reuters the present leadership had led the movement into isolation.

"Hamas has made mistakes. The leadership of Hamas in Gaza failed to adapt to new changes after the peace process. It hesitated and was not brave enough to make decisions, so we demand that it step down and give new blood a chance to lead," one member said.

"We need a new pragmatic, qualified leadership to lead a new Hamas with a new programme. If they want us to continue armed struggle or not, we will follow it but we must have a clear vision and answers," another Hamas man said.
Some activists said they wanted to abandon militancy, terming anti-Israel violence a mistake that led to confrontation with the Palestinian Authority and Israel and to international condemnation.
What is needed, they said, is a new pragmatic and peaceful policy.
One of Hamas' traditional leaders confirmed the movement lacked a clear strategy but said it was difficult to chart a straight course in a region that is "like quicksand".
